doc.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018

title: Teaching artist work and a family of teachers
summary: She loves teaching; her mother and grandmother were educators.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I shared something with you that we both did and that is being a teaching artist. Is that amazing work?

I love it. Well I’ve been told that teaching is in my blood. My mother is a teacher, my grandmother was a teacher, an educator, a professor, but also a nurse. And she was a head nurse to teach other nurses. And education is just really important. It was important to me. It changed my life. And I really love watching that moment when things click, and even helping someone through when you’re hitting that wall. And it’s just like uh — and we all experience that every day with something, especially if we’re brave enough to try to get better at something. So I like being a part of that.
